attempted_claim: Let X4 be CP^2 blown up at four general points with its monotone symplectic form, and let S be the explicit Lagrangian sphere in class E1 - E2. Let L be the explicitly named Vianna triangular monotone torus fibre in a fixed almost-toric base diagram of X4, with Maslov-2 disk potential WL and pearl complex. Is L relatively non-displaceable from S, meaning every Hamiltonian image of L intersects S, certified by nonvanishing mixed Lagrangian Floer homology HF^*(L, S; rho) for an explicit rank-one local system rho on L computed via a pearl-strip complex? A complete answer proves or disproves this by constructing L and S explicitly in disjoint-versus-intersecting position, writing WL and solving dWL = 0, computing the pearl differential on L with rho and the mixed differential counting strips between L and S, and either establishing the nonvanishing obstruction or exhibiting an explicit Hamiltonian with phi(L) disjoint from S plus the vanishing computation.
claim_type: relative torus-sphere non-displaceability via mixed Floer
decisive_failure: Lane inputs fix no almost-toric base diagram coordinates, nodal data, or matching-cycle embedding for S, so neither the Vianna fibre position nor L∩S can be audited; the mixed pearl-strip differential needs regular-J transversality, compactness, gluing and rho-weighted strip counts far beyond bounded in-lane computation. The only completed check is a model-potential critical-point computation that does not touch the mixed differential.
